**v1.10.0: the bot's window and Wizard101 can go to the tray instead of closing (two new settings, both off), the dashboard gets a menu bar, and your settings can be saved to a file and loaded back.**
- **The bot's window in the tray** (`traybot`, off by default; new, and not tried in the game yet). Switch it on in Settings > THE MOUSE AND WAITS, "Put the bot's window in the tray". Then the dashboard's X (Alt+F4 in it too) and its minimize button put it in the tray instead of stopping the bot - the bot plays on. Double-click the tray icon (the tray menu's new "Show the bot's window") or press Windows+2 to bring it back; while it's on, that double-click no longer switches walking on/off. The tray menu's "Exit" (or Windows+Esc) stops the bot, and a tray tip says so the first time. Off: the X stops the bot, as before.
- **Wizard101 in the tray** (`traygame`, off by default; new, and not tried in the game yet). Settings > THE MOUSE AND WAITS, "Put Wizard101 in the tray". Then Alt+F4 with Wizard101 in front, a click on its own X and its minimize button hide its window in the tray - the game keeps running, its taskbar button goes, and nothing is sent into it. The X and minimize only when it's windowed (a title bar): a borderless or exclusive full screen game minimizes as ever. The tray menu's new "Show Wizard101" brings it back to the front. It also comes back by itself, without taking the focus (minimized if it was), when you switch the setting off, when the bot closes (Windows+Esc, Exit, a restart, an update), and - if the bot ended without that (End task, a crash) - at the bot's next start or from the "Open with Wizard101" watcher.
- **The bot is off while Wizard101 is in the tray.** Sending it there lets go of every key and switches the bot off as F6 does - each round and walking stop, and a click or key press it had under way is dropped, never sent to another window - and brings the bot back on once the game is back, if it was on. Meanwhile the bot can't be switched on, and the tray menu's "Buy potions now", "Record potion buying..." and quick sell say "show Wizard101 first"; nothing brings the game forward by itself, and the dashboard says "Wizard101 is in the tray". It isn't sent there - a tray tip says why - with two Wizard101 windows open, while auto-reconnect is getting it back online, or during a potion run, potion recording or quick sell you started. If the game closes while hidden, the bot sees it closed as ever. A restart (Windows+1) or an update while it's in the tray shows it again and starts the bot off: F6 starts it.
- **What can't be caught** still really closes the game, as before: the taskbar's "Close window", the X on a taskbar thumbnail or in Alt+Tab, Close in the window's own menu (Alt+Space), Task Manager and the game's own Quit. A click on its X while the bot is too busy to check it in time closes it too. With these on, minimizing every window (Windows+M) sends the dashboard and a windowed Wizard101 to the tray too.
- **The dashboard's menu bar** (new, and not tried in the game yet). File, Bot, View, Settings and Help sit at the window's top left, and Alt+F, B, V, T and H open them (Settings is Alt+T, because Alt+S is Statistic mode's key while the bot is on). File: "Save settings as...", "Load settings from..." (below), "Open bot folder", "Open debug.log", "Exit" (the bot stops). Bot: "Bot on/off", "Walking on/off", "Play for me", "Wait for me", "Bring Wizard101 to the front" and "Show Wizard101" (there to pick only while Wizard101 is in the tray). View: "Map", "Simple view", "Log colours...", "Pause log", "Clear log", "Overlay". Settings: "Settings...", "Put the bot's window in the tray", "Put Wizard101 in the tray", "Discord alerts...", "Party...", "Wizard101 login...". Help: "Check for updates", "Report a bug...", "Read me" (README.txt in Notepad), "About" (the version and the name of the folder AutoFarmer is in). Each item that was a button, or is in the tray menu too, does the same as that. Every pick is logged, like "Menu: Bot > Play for me picked". While one of its menus is open the bot waits, as it does while the tray menu is open - pick an item or press Esc and it goes on.
- **Which buttons moved where.** At the top right, Report a bug and Check for updates are now Help > "Report a bug..." and Help > "Check for updates". On the Bot tab, Settings is Settings > "Settings...", Map is View > "Map" and Colours (over the log) is View > "Log colours...". From the bottom row: Pause log, Clear and Open debug.log are View > "Pause log" (ticked while the log is paused - the button said "Resume log"), View > "Clear log" and File > "Open debug.log"; Walking on/off and Wait for me are in the Bot menu, Game to front is Bot > "Bring Wizard101 to the front" (the tray menu's name for it), Open bot folder is in the File menu, and the Advanced view / Simple view button is View > "Simple view" (ticked while it's simple). The bot on/off button stays on the window, now at the top right where Check for updates was ("Bot: on (F6)" / "Bot: off (F6)"); Play for me stays on the tab row, and each tab keeps its own buttons.
- **Ticks, keys and "Update to v...".** A tick shows what's on now, however it was switched - the menu, a button, F6, F8, Windows+4, the tray menu or the Settings window - within a second: the bot, walking, Play for me, Wait for me, the game brought to the front (ticked with Play for me on too, which brings it up whatever `gamefront` says), the map, the simple view, the log paused, the overlay and the two tray settings. "Pause log" and "Clear log" are greyed in the simple view, which shows no log. An item with a key shows it at its right, in brackets - "(F6)" - and follows the Keys tab. "Check for updates" says "Checking..." and is greyed for 10 s after a click. While a newer version is out, "Update to v..." sits at the bar's right end, as the Updates button said it, and a click on it checks for updates.
- **The tray settings from the menu.** Settings > "Put the bot's window in the tray" and "Put Wizard101 in the tray" switch `traybot` and `traygame` and save them at once, as the Settings window's Save does (an open Settings window shows the change too): debug.log "Menu: traybot 0 -> 1". If PlayerStats.txt can't be written, a tray tip says "Couldn't save that setting - PlayerStats.txt couldn't be written."
- **The window.** With the bottom row of buttons gone, the log reaches the window's bottom. The simple view is as tall inside as before (330 at the least - the menu bar makes it about 20 taller on the screen); a simple view's size saved before is kept. The advanced view, saved by an older version, comes back about as tall on the screen as it was: 20 less inside, for the menu bar (a new one opens 784 high, was 804). Where the bot places the window or fits it to the monitor, it allows for the menu bar, so the window's bottom stays clear of the taskbar.
- **Settings in a file of your own** (new, and not tried in the game yet). File > "Save settings as..." writes the Settings window's settings, as they're in use now, to a text file - to keep, or for another PC (it offers Documents and "Wiz-Maxxing settings <date>.txt"; .txt is added to a name without one). Its first line says which version saved it and when; then each setting is a `key:value` line with its label, under the Settings window's headings. For the mobs' reach (`mobradius`, `mobbody`) it writes what you last set in Settings, if you did - not what the bot widened it to since. Never in it: your stats, the cards the bot learned, the settings kept only in PlayerStats.txt (`navmem`...), the network PIN (`netpin`), the Discord webhook and the Wizard101 login (those two are kept in Windows Credential Manager, never in a file) - nor your keys, decks, dungeon runs, the windows' places or party.ini. It won't write over PlayerStats.txt, dashboard.ini or party.ini in the bot's folder. debug.log: "Settings saved in <file> - N settings (not the network PIN)" - a file's name only, never where it is.
- **Loading shows you first.** File > "Load settings from..." reads such a file - or a plain PlayerStats.txt from another PC, of which only the Settings window's settings are taken. Each value is checked as the Settings window checks it, and a window lists each setting the file would change, with its value now and the file's; every one is ticked but the party's two (`partyrole`, `partybattle`: this PC's own part). Notes under the list say what isn't loaded - a value a setting can't take, keys that aren't in the Settings window (stats, learned cards, settings kept only in PlayerStats.txt such as `navmem`, a newer version's: "Saved by a newer bot (...)" says so), lines it couldn't read, a network PIN - what was brought into its range, and what still wins over a loaded setting: the deck in use's own value or a wizard's own line for its school (`storm.killmargin`...), and Wait for me's reset at every start. Apply first copies PlayerStats.txt to backups\ ("PlayerStats before settings load <date time>.txt"; if that copy fails, nothing is loaded), then sets the ticked ones, used at once with no restart. A setting the file doesn't have stays as it is; Cancel, the window's X or Esc changes nothing. Not while the Settings window is open: "Close the Settings window first - then load the settings." debug.log: "Settings loaded from <file>: key old -> new, ... | PlayerStats.txt as it was: backups\...".
- **The Settings window's Save** goes the same way now. Its debug.log line is "Settings: key old -> new, ..." (it was "Settings saved (used from now on): ..."), and a "Bring Wizard101 to the front" (`gamefront`) changed there now ticks the tray menu's item and the Bot menu's at once - before, the tray menu's tick and the dashboard's Game to front button stayed as they were.
- **The network PIN stays out of debug.log.** A `netpin` changed in the Settings window is now logged as "netpin changed", never its numbers, and "Report a bug..." blanks a PIN in older debug.log lines ("netpin 0 -> 1234", as the Save logged it before). The end of debug.log goes into a public bug report.
- **Not tried in the game yet.** The bot's side was only read, not run (no AutoHotkey or Windows where it was made). AutoFarmer\LIVE_CHECKS.txt step 3.12 says what to try with the tray - each way in and out, Alt+F4 in the middle of a battle round, the bot closing and starting again with the game in the tray, two game windows - and step 3.13 with the menu bar and a settings file saved and loaded back (one setting changed, a file from a newer version, every way to cancel); both say what to send. memclicks is now step 3.14, still last.
- **Updating:** the updater offers this to every install, including ones set up from the v0.7.0 or v0.7.1 zips. Your settings, learned cards and routes are kept. A copy run from the code: git pull.
